newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Western Australia okays RTZ-CRA iron ore mine.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Western Australia okays RTZ-CRA iron ore mine.

text.p: The Western Australia government said on Thursday it has reached an agreement with RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd subsidiary Hamersley Iron Pty Ltd to develop a new mine that will initially produce up to 15 million tonnes of iron ore a year.
Subject to approval from RTZ-CRA, construction of the mine would start in 1997, with production of iron ore commencing in 1999, state Resources Development Minister Colin Barnett said.
The mine would be located at Yandicoogina, 90 km northwest of the town of Newman in the Pilbara region of the state, and would cost A$400 million to develop, he said in a statement.
Depending on future demand for iron ore, output from the mine could double to about 30 million tonnes annually, Barnett said.

The agreement also details an obligation on Hamersley's part to build a "metallised agglomerate plant" once the mine has been operating for 10 years or produced 150 million tonnes of iron ore, Barnett said.
RTZ-CRA has been researching technology into the commercial viability of building a plant employing the HIsmelt smelting process, which produces high-carbon molten iron from low-cost iron ore fines.

Rival mining company, The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, has already started construction of an iron ore plant in Port Hedland, Western Australia, using separate technology developed in Venezuela. It expects to start production of iron in the form of hot briquettes in less than a year.
The initial term of the mining lease will be 21 years, although the agreement gives Hamersley the right to two successive renewals of 21 years each, the statement said.
Under Western Australia law, mining companies lease land from the state for mining.
The agreement also allows for the construction of an 87 km railway to serve the mine, the statement said.
Hamersley currently produces about 55 million tonnes of iron ore a year, a company spokesman said.
The Yandi deposit is a high-grade, low impurity iron ore ore ideally suited for blast furnace feed, he said.
He said Hamersley has committed to a further two years research on the HIsmelt process, bringing its total investment in the project to about A$310 million.
